summary: Streaming ack-window interaction causes reordered and replayed tool/function side-effects under concurrent retries
description: Customer reports duplicate side-effects and apparent out-of-order execution of downstream tool calls when using streaming function-calls with client-side concurrency + backpressure. Behavior reproduced against Dedicated pool in us-west-2. Customer uses long confirmation/ack window on webhook side (up to 10s) and concurrent request batching on their orchestrator which retries stalled streams. Several tool calls that should be idempotent are executed twice and, on retries, sometimes appear applied in a different order than the original intent.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Client opens streaming chat session using Python SDK v0.9.2 with function_call enabled.
2) Orchestrator issues two parallel prompts that both trigger function A then function B in fast succession (concurrent streams multiplexed).
3) Customer webhook acknowledges function execution with an ack token but intentionally delays final confirmation up to 8-10s (to simulate heavy backend processing).
4) When ack not received within ack-window, client retries the streaming session / reconnects and the SDK / server retries function calls per default retry policy.
5) Observe downstream system shows function A executed twice for request 1, and in one of the retries function B runs before function A for request 2 (ordering flipped).
observed_behavior: Duplicate executions of server-invoked functions (webhook receives the same tool call twice) and occasional reordering of function calls across retries under concurrent multiplexing. Customer sees side-effects like duplicate DB inserts and inventory adjustments applied out-of-order.
expected_behavior: At-most-once or at-least-once semantics documented per SDK for streaming function calls depending on idempotency keys, but ordering across independent concurrent streams should be preserved per-request and retries should not reorder within a single logical request. Duplicate tool calls should be avoidable when idempotency keys are provided and respected by server-side retry logic.
logs: 2026-03-09T14:12:07Z INFO tool/invoke tool=funcA request=abc123 idempotency_key= (missing) -- duplicate
2026-03-09T14:12:08Z INFO tool/invoke tool=funcA request=def456 -- observed ordering mismatch (A after B)
comments: 2026-03-10 — Aisha Patel: Opened ticket after reproducing with Neptune's QA harness. Customer concerned about duplicate billing events and incorrect inventory counts.
2026-03-10 — Markus Chen: Acknowledged; requesting full request logs and webhook headers. Asked customer to share SDK request IDs and sample payloads.

2026-03-11 — Customer (Neptune SRE, Jorge Ramos): Provided sample bundle (s3://neptune-prod/bugs/ack-window-bundle.zip) and timeline. Noted they intentionally delay final webhook confirm to simulate long-running downstream work.

2026-03-11 — Markus Chen: Noted absence of idempotency keys in tool calls in logs and asked whether SDK should auto-generate session-scoped idempotency. Assigned to runtime/serving to check retry surface area.

2026-03-12 — Runtime Eng (Elena Ruiz): Confirmed we saw duplicate invocations when streaming reconnect occurs and ack window exceeded. Hypothesis: reconnection + server-side retry path does not canonicalize idempotency when client did not provide explicit per-invocation idempotency key.
2026-03-12 — Support (Markus Chen): Added temporary mitigation guidance for customer and recommended SDK upgrade path and server config change.
investigation_notes: Checked server traces: reconnection path emits 'resend_pending_calls' for sessions with unacked tool calls.

Replay shows no normalized idempotency key was attached to per-tool invocation for multiplexed concurrent calls; server retry uses session-level token only and cannot deduplicate across reconnections.

Observed race between resend and in-flight 'delivery confirmation' path resulting in second invoke where first invoke later completes — leads to duplicates but also to crossover ordering when mixes of retried and original calls interleave.
SDKs differ: TS SDK (1.3.0) automatically attaches per-call nonce when function_call invoked in single-threaded path; Python/Go SDKs rely on user to pass idempotency_key or higher-level session flag.
No evidence of bug in customer's webhook. Root cause looks to be missing per-invocation idempotency coupling to server-side dedupe and race during reconnect under concurrent streams.
resolution: Mitigation provided: (1) Customer temporarily increased webhook confirmation aggressiveness to emit idempotency_key per tool invocation (or echoed session+sequence) and suppressed client-side reconnect retries for 15s to allow confirmation path to complete; (2) Support recommended upgrading Python SDK to 0.10.x which includes automatic per-call nonce generation when function_call is used concurrently, and applying server-side patch that normalizes idempotency headers on reconnection (PR #1428). Follow-ups: runtime team to backport dedupe logic to dedicated pools (ENG-1428), SDK team to document idempotency patterns in README and add guardrails for sessions with long ack windows.
